niche.habitat: Liquid outer core boundary layer (approx. 2,900 km depth)
niche.diet: Magnetic shear and convective entropy gradients

body: Highly speculative fantasy: gossamer helical filaments of self-organizing iron-sulfur plasma; 10-50 km in length; no fixed mass, just persistent pattern. No carbon chemistry or solvent exists here.

skill.effect: The creature rides invisible magnetic currents, moving strongly and swiftly while completely ignoring any magnetic interference, allowing it to navigate freely.

chains.weakness: Magnetic shear tears it apart if the field reverses abruptly.

journal.en: A ghost woven from iron and thought.

plausibility.summary: Either file it explicitly as a non-living dynamo pattern (F23 fantasy tier) that the player observes or avoids as a hazard, never commands, or move the grazer into the fracture aquifer (0.9-4 km, F12, F20): rebuild it as a colony of magnetotactic iron-sulfur microbes with encoded magnetosomes, rooted in F6 plus F15 redox below 118 C. Keep the fun as 'Magnetic Ride' (Control): a field-aligned glide that gathers the colony and steadies its compass. Weakness: an abrupt field reversal scrambles the magnetosomes.

analogues.organism: Magnetotactic bacteria (e.g., Magnetospirillum) orient in Earth's field using intracellular magnetite magnetosomes — a real solution, but it requires a cell, water and metabolism; nothing analogous survives core conditions.

links: Harvests work from fluid velocity shear

Core is above 300 GPa and 5000 K

skill.effect: The creature draws warmth from the surrounding currents, sapping strength from nearby targets while restoring its own vitality, leaving a visible trail of condensed heat.

chains.weakness: Starves in laminar flow regions; cannot persist without shear.
observe: Glows faintly where flow is turbulent
No intake orifice, dissolves into flow

journal.en: It eats the wind of the world's heart.

plausibility.summary: Re-root it as a chemosynthetic grazer at a redox interface in the aquifer (F15, F19, F20, at or below 118 C): it harvests H2 / Fe(II)-sulfate disequilibrium, with Darcy flow (F12) and calcite sealing (F16) deciding where the interface sits. Keep the luminous, shape-shifting look as filaments brightest where mixing is fastest. 'Entropy Siphon' (Poke): a single burst of stored radiolytic oxygen (F22) spent on one feeding strike. Weakness: in stagnant brine the redux front is sealed by calcite and it starves. If it stays in the core, call it a pattern, not a feeder — drop consume/heal verbs entirely.

analogues.organism: No organism metabolises entropy or shear. Vent chemoautotrophs (e.g., the symbionts of Riftia pachyptila) exploit chemical disequilibrium, and bacteria sense flow through mechanosensitive channels, but both are aqueous, low-temperature chemistry — the opposite of core matter.

chains.trait: Synchronizes oscillation to the 56-hour tidal month
links: Tidal strain modulates core convection velocity
Creature locks phase to maximize shear harvest

skill.effect: The creature strikes strongly with amplified force whenever it senses the player entering a specific rhythm, making its attacks noticeably more powerful.

chains.weakness: Disoriented during the 'slack' tide; attack chance -50%.

journal.en: The planet's heartbeat is its clock.

links: Uses sound to phase-lock with distant herds

skill.effect: Syncs with other creatures, +2 to group rolls, shares status effects.

chains.weakness: Loud sound attracts 'Dynamo grazers' that disrupt flow; stealth is impossible.
observe: Constant low hum recorded by seismometers

journal.en: A choir of iron singing in the dark.

body_plan.origin: Emergent MHD instability at the liquid-solid boundary

temperament: Aloof, rhythmic, indifferent to solid matter
secrets: It leaves isotopic fractionation in mantle plumes.
Its 'song' can be used to stabilize unstable fractures.
moments: A ripple in the seismic data resolves into a massive, slow-turning helix, its 'heartbeat' perfectly matching the tidal clock.

journal.en: Highly speculative fantasy: a self-organizing MHD pattern with no copying mechanism, yet it dances.
We measure its mass in joules and its age in magnetic cycles.
